hints.title: Negative and Trailing Zero Elimination
hints.text: Negative integers cannot read identically in reverse because the minus sign appears only at the start. How can reversing just the second half of digits check symmetry without converting to a string?

hints.title: Half Digit Reversal Invariant
hints.text: When reversing digits from right to left, stopping when reversed half becomes greater than or equal to the remaining half avoids integer overflow.

hints.title: Half Integer Reversal Comparison Procedure
hints.text: If x is negative or ends in zero with x non-zero, return false immediately. Build the reversed number by repeatedly extracting x modulo 10 and dividing x by 10 until x is less than or equal to reversed. Check if x equals reversed or reversed integer divided by 10.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(log N) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Converting numbers to strings incurs heap allocation and violates the optional constraint of constant space.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Reversing half the digits takes O(log10 N) time and O(1) auxiliary space while completely avoiding overflow.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should avoid string conversion, handle negative numbers, and cleanly compare odd-length digit counts.
